newsitem.title: UK: S&P affirms France's Haut-Rhin debt rating.
newsitem.headline: S&P affirms France's Haut-Rhin debt rating.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Thursday it affirmed its AA plus senior unsecured debt rating of the department of Haut-Rhin.
The outlook was stable, S&P said in a statement.

"The rating is based on Haut-Rhin's diverse and developing economy, as well as on its robust operating performance and healthy financial flexibility, which will allow the financing of an important capital program with a limited increase in debt levels," said S&P.
Haut-Rhin, in the Alsace region of north-east France, is a relatively wealthy department, with an above average GDP per inhabitant, S&P said.

Industry occupies a central place in the local economy, although it is slowly giving way to the rapidly developing tertiary sector. Haut-Rhin has been hit less by the economic downturn in France than other French departments, as evidenced by an unemployment rate four to six percentage points below the national average, S&P said. After a short period of recovery at the end of 1994 and early 1995, Haut-Rhin's economy has, since mid-1995, slowed down again in line with France and other Western European countries. The department, nevertheless, remains in a relatively favourable position, as illustrated by the continuous decline in its unemployment rate to 6.9 percent in March 1996, whereas the national average increased back to 12.7 percent, S&P said.

Haut-Rhin reports comfortable operating surpluses each year, despite a slight decline since 1991, S&P said. Tax revenues are increasing steadily, in line with the department's strong tax base growth (more than 3.5 percnet p.a. since 1990), while tax rates have remained stable well below the national average, S&P said.

Operating expenditures are growing slightly faster than revenues, reflecting the pressure of social care spending. But the department managed to limit spending rises in 1994 and 1995 thanks to tighter controls. Capital spending will rise to 40 percent of total expenditure in 1996, up from 36 percent in 1994 and 1995 as an important program for the reconstruction of junior highschools begins. Consequently, direct debt, which represented 79 percent of adjusted operating revenues at year-end 1995, will continue to rise marginally until this program is completed by 1998, but should remain manageable, S&P said.
Haut-Rhin's economy will continue to grow thanks to its structural strengths, and its ability to attract new companies from neighbouring regions of France, Germany, and Switzerland.
Steady revenue growth and a tight control on spending will enable the department to carry through its capital program without large debt accumulation, S&P said.
